name: Creation to the Flood (Genesis 1-11)

objectives.text: Identify God as the maker of everything in the creation account, including the first man and woman, Adam and Eve
Retell the story of Noah and the ark in order using pictures or toys
Name what God made on each of the six days of creation and that He rested on the seventh day
Identify the rainbow as the sign of God's promise never again to destroy the earth by a flood
Retell how Adam and Eve disobeyed God in the garden, naming the command God gave and what they chose to do
Describe what happened between the brothers Cain and Abel and how God responded to Cain
Explain how the consequences God announced after the Fall changed life for people and for the world
Describe how God formed the woman and joined her to the man as the first marriage
Sequence the major events of Genesis 1-11 from Creation through the Fall, Cain and Abel, the Flood, and Babel
Explain why God sent the Flood as judgment on human wickedness and why He spared Noah and his family
Describe the events at the Tower of Babel and explain why God confused the languages and scattered the people
Explain what Genesis teaches about humans being made in the image of God, using both the creation account and the command after the Flood
Identify Shem, Ham, and Japheth as the sons of Noah from whom the nations of the earth descended
Compare God's commands to Adam with His commands to Noah to show how the creation mandate is renewed after the Flood
Analyze the repeated pattern in the genealogy from Adam to Noah, including the refrain of death and the exception of Enoch
Explain the covenant God made with Noah by identifying its parties, promises, and sign
Analyze the spread of sin across the narratives of Genesis 3-11 from the garden to Babel
Contrast the line of Cain with the line of Seth as presented in Genesis 4-5
Interpret the Table of Nations as an account of the common descent of all peoples from Noah's family
Connect the scattering of languages at Babel with the gathering of the nations at Pentecost and in the Great Commission
Explain Genesis 3:15 as the first gospel promise and trace its fulfillment in Christ through the New Testament
Analyze how the repeated heading these are the generations organizes Genesis 1-11 and links Adam to Abraham
Explain how the Flood narrative presents an undoing and renewal of creation by tracing its parallels with Genesis 1
Compare the Genesis creation and flood accounts with ancient Near Eastern accounts such as Enuma Elish and Gilgamesh to identify how Genesis presents God and humanity differently
Evaluate the major interpretations of the sons of God and the daughters of man in Genesis 6 using the text and its context
Evaluate interpretations of the days of creation held within the Reformed tradition in light of the text and the confession's statement of creation in the space of six days
Construct an argument for the tradition's historical reading of Adam and the Flood using how later Scripture refers to these events
Synthesize the themes of creation, judgment, and grace in Genesis 1-11 into an account of how these chapters prepare for God's call of Abraham

changes: Kept and reworded real competencies (creator, Noah retelling, Cain and Abel, consequences of sin, sequence, reason for the Flood, sons of Noah, spread of sin, Table of Nations, Babel and Pentecost, Genesis 3:15, sons of God, historicity, synthesis). Dropped the vague before-and-after Flood comparison and the genealogy timeline, replacing them with a creation-mandate comparison and a Genesis 5 pattern analysis. Added days of creation, rainbow sign, the Fall narrative, marriage, image of God, Noahic covenant, Cain and Seth lines, toledot structure, de-creation in the Flood, ancient Near Eastern comparison, and Reformed views of the creation days. Replaced whole-chapter or vague references with specific verses and added only confessional articles that state each doctrine.
